text: The patient presented to our emergency department with a three-day history of dyspnea and chest pain.
The ECG showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 130 beats per minute.
We started anticoagulation with apixaban and achieved rate control with bisoprolol.
Laboratory studies showed a CRP of 85 and a leukocytosis with a white count of 14 per nanoliter.
The chest X-ray confirmed a right lower lobe pneumonia with an associated pleural effusion.
Empiric antibiotic therapy was given with piperacillin and tazobactam for seven days.
In known type 2 diabetes mellitus, the HbA1c remains above target.
spoken: In known type 2 diabetes mellitus, the H B A 1 C remains above target.

text: We recommend adding empagliflozin to the existing metformin.
His hypertension is well controlled on ramipril and amlodipine.
Echocardiography revealed mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function.
The NT-proBNP was markedly elevated, consistent with decompensated heart failure.
spoken: The N T pro B N P was markedly elevated, consistent with decompensated heart failure.

text: Intravenous furosemide led to good diuresis with a weight loss of four kilograms.
Upper endoscopy demonstrated reflux esophagitis and erosive gastritis in the antrum.
We prescribed pantoprazole 40 milligrams once daily for eight weeks.
The rapid test for Helicobacter pylori was positive, so eradication therapy was initiated.
At colonoscopy, a two-centimeter polyp in the sigmoid colon was completely removed.
Histology showed a tubulovillous adenoma without evidence of malignancy.
She reports recurrent episodes of vertigo and one episode of syncope on standing.
A Holter monitor showed no significant arrhythmias and no pauses.
Thyroid function tests showed a suppressed TSH with an elevated free T4, consistent with hyperthyroidism.
We initiated antithyroid treatment with methimazole.
For hypothyroidism, the dose of levothyroxine was increased to 75 micrograms.
CT of the abdomen showed acute sigmoid diverticulitis without perforation.
Antibiotics were continued orally with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole.
Ultrasound showed cholelithiasis with a thickened gallbladder wall.
We recommend an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy once she is symptom-free.
Lipase was five times the upper limit of normal, so we suspect acute pancreatitis.
Renal function is impaired with a creatinine of 2 and an eGFR of 35.

text: Given this renal insufficiency, metformin should be held and the sitagliptin dose reduced.
Potassium was 6, so spironolactone was discontinued.
Because a pulmonary embolism was suspected, a CT angiogram of the pulmonary arteries was performed.
The D-dimer was elevated, and duplex ultrasound confirmed a left deep vein thrombosis.
Therapeutic anticoagulation was started with enoxaparin and then switched to rivaroxaban.
The patient has GOLD stage 3 COPD with frequent exacerbations.
His inhaled therapy consists of tiotropium and formoterol, with albuterol as needed.
We gave prednisone 40 milligrams for five days without a taper.
Spirometry showed a moderate obstructive ventilatory defect.
She complains of paresthesias in both feet, consistent with diabetic polyneuropathy.
For the neuropathic pain we started pregabalin with gradual titration.
MRI of the brain showed acute ischemic lesions in the left middle cerebral artery territory.
After thrombolysis with alteplase, the right-sided hemiparesis partially resolved.
For secondary prevention he receives clopidogrel and atorvastatin 80 milligrams.
His Parkinson's disease medication with carbidopa and levodopa is continued unchanged.
She takes levetiracetam 500 milligrams twice daily for epilepsy.
The radiograph showed a displaced distal radius fracture on the right.
Open reduction and internal fixation with a volar plate was performed under a brachial plexus block.
For analgesia she received acetaminophen and oxycodone as needed.
Bone densitometry showed osteoporosis, and we recommend alendronate and cholecalciferol.
The complete blood count showed iron deficiency anemia with a hemoglobin of 9 and a low ferritin.
We gave intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and scheduled an upper endoscopy for further workup.
She has recurrent major depressive disorder and takes escitalopram and mirtazapine.
For nighttime agitation related to dementia he receives low-dose quetiapine.
The urinary tract infection was treated with a single dose of fosfomycin.
Pyelonephritis was suspected, and the urine culture grew Escherichia coli.
Serial troponins were negative, making an acute coronary syndrome unlikely.
Cardiac catheterization revealed a significant stenosis of the left anterior descending artery.
A drug-eluting stent was placed, and dual antiplatelet therapy continues with ticagrelor.
Her rheumatoid arthritis is in remission on methotrexate and folic acid.
Please recheck liver function tests, in particular the GGT and bilirubin, in four weeks.

text: The patient is discharged in improved general condition to the care of her primary care physician.
